input.command: cd site && ls . css js && grep -n "orders\|table\|th\b\|td\|tr" css/*.css | head -60
sed -n 290,335p css/components.css; sed -n 460,500p css/components.css; grep -n "table" orders.html css/pages.css | head -20
grep -n "class=\"table\"" *.html; grep -n "space-" css/tokens.css; sed -n 60,75p orders.html; grep -n "td\|tr\b" css/pages.css

sed -i '64s/class="table"/class="table table-compact"/' orders.html
python3 - <<'E'
p='css/components.css'
s=open(p).read()
a=".table tbody tr:last-child td {"
s=s.replace(a,".table-compact tbody td {\n  padding-top: 6px;\n  padding-bottom: 6px;\n}\n\n"+a,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
cd .. && (npx playwright test tests/functional.spec.ts 2>&1 | tail -8; npx playwright test tests/visual.spec.ts 2>&1 | tail -15)

content.text:
Orders table rows are now more compact, with 6px of padding above and below the text. The heading row is unchanged.

- **Change:** I added a `table-compact` class to the orders table in `site/orders.html` and a `.table-compact tbody td` rule in `site/css/components.css`. The pricing page uses the same table component, so I scoped the change to the orders table and left pricing alone.
- **Functional tests:** all 16 pass.
- **Visual tests:** the two orders screenshots (desktop and phone) now fail, as expected, because the rows are shorter. The other 10 pass, including pricing. I looked at the new desktop render and it looks right: tighter rows, heading row as before.
- **Not done:** I haven't updated the approved screenshots. Once you're happy with the new look, I can regenerate the two orders baselines.

STATUS: DONE
